1.title: ARM Templates and Bicep
1.text: Welcome to Module seven: A R M Templates and Bicep. It covers the exam area Deploy and manage Azure compute resources. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Interpret an Azure Resource Manager template or a Bicep file. Modify an existing template. Modify an existing Bicep file. Deploy resources by using a template or a Bicep file. Export a deployment as a template or convert a template to a Bicep file. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources (twenty-twenty-five percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft Learn A Z-one hundred four study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-six, two thousand twenty-three.

1.title: Infrastructure as code with Azure Resource Manager
1.text: Infrastructure as code with Azure Resource Manager. Azure Resource Manager (A R M) is the management layer that handles every request to create, update or delete Azure resources (portal, C L I, Power Shell, S D Ks all go through it). An A R M (Azure Resource Manager) template is a Jason file that declares the resources you want. Properties.

1.title: Infrastructure as code with Azure Resource Manager, continued
1.text: Infrastructure as code with Azure Resource Manager. Declarative. You describe what you want, not the steps. Idempotent. Deploying the same template repeatedly gives the same result. Repeatable. The same template builds dev, test and production with different parameters.

1.title: Infrastructure as code with Azure Resource Manager, continued
1.text: Infrastructure as code with Azure Resource Manager. The figure shows this: The A R M template sections and how a deployment flows through Azure Resource Manager.

1.title: Template structure
1.text: Template structure. schema, content Version. Required header. parameters. Input values at deploy time (name, size, password). variables. Reusable values inside the template. resources. The Azure resources to deploy. outputs. Values returned after deployment (for example a connection string). depends On makes one resource wait for another; A R M also infers dependencies from references. Template functions such as concat, resource Group and parameters build values.

1.title: Bicep
1.text: Bicep. Bicep is a simpler language that compiles to A R M templates. It has cleaner syntax, automatic dependency handling, modules, and the same capabilities. Convert to Bicep. A Z bicep decompile the file flag template dot json turns an A R M template into Bicep. Convert to A R M. A Z bicep build the file flag main dot bicep produces the Jason. Parameters. param location string resource Group dot location. Existing resource. The existing keyword refers to a resource already deployed. Modules. Split large deployments into reusable files. Exam tip: Bicep and A R M templates are two ways to do the same thing; Bicep is the shorter one and compiles to A R M.

1.title: Deploying
1.text: Deploying. Commands. A Z deployment group create (resource group scope), A Z deployment sub create, or Power Shell New Az Resource Group Deployment. Scopes. Resource group, subscription, management group, tenant. Incremental mode (default). Adds or updates the resources in the template; leaves other resources alone. Complete mode. Deletes resources in the resource group that are not in the template. What-if. Previews changes before deploying. Parameter file. A Jason file with values for the template parameters. Exam tip: Complete mode can delete resources that are not in the template. Use what-if first.

1.title: Exporting and modifying
1.text: Exporting and modifying. Export a deployment as a template. Portal: Automation greater than Export template on a resource group, a resource or a deployment. Modify. Edit the Jason or Bicep (change a parameter default, skew, location), then redeploy. Template spec. Store a versioned template in Azure for others to deploy. Exported templates often need clean-up (some resources or secrets are not exported). Exam tip: Incremental mode (the default) never deletes; complete mode deletes resources that are not in the template.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Which template section lets a user supply a V M name at deployment time? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: parameters. Parameters take input values at deployment.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A team deploys with complete mode and resources disappear. What happened? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Complete mode deleted resources in the resource group that were not in the template. Complete mode removes resources that are not in the template.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which command converts an A R M template into Bicep? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A Z bicep decompile. Decompile turns Jason into Bicep; build does the opposite.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. An administrator wants to preview what a deployment would change before running it. What should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: What-if. What-if shows the planned changes.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. What does it mean that A R M templates are idempotent? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Deploying the same template repeatedly gives the same result. Repeated deployments produce the same state.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. An administrator wants a template of an existing resource group to recreate it elsewhere. What can be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Export template. Export template generates a template from existing resources.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What language is an A R M template written in? Answer: Jason. Question two. What does Bicep compile to? Answer: An A R M template. Question three. Which deployment mode is the default? Answer: Incremental.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the outputs section for? Answer: Returning values after deployment. Question five. Name the template deployment scopes. Answer: Resource group, subscription, management group and tenant. Question six. What does a template spec store? Answer: A versioned template for others to deploy.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. A R M template: Jason; declarative, idempotent; parameters, variables, resources, outputs. Bicep: simpler; compiles to A R M; decompile or build; modules. Deploy: A Z deployment group create; incremental (default) versus complete; what-if. Export: export template from group, resource or deployment.
